prompts.master: Use case: stylized-concept. Generate ONE complete horizontal 3:1 panoramic SIDE-VIEW 2D PIXEL-ART GAME SCENE, a visual-direction MASTER candidate for 'Rusty Crossings'. Not a collage, diagram, map, infographic or UI. Use input1 ONLY for rusted steel/rail/weathered material cues, NOT its bridge layout; use input2 ONLY for organic bank/foliage/water motifs. The actual stage is an ALGORITHMIC MAZE made from interconnected rusted horizontal and vertical metal bars, right-angle turns, staggered shelves, branching passages, short dead ends, vertical shafts and loops. It should evoke tracing a pathfinding search through a maze as a side-scrolling exploration/action space, NOT one bridge over a river or a rail parkour shortcut. Dominant readable maze fills middle/right two thirds of the complete scene, with large negative-space passages between bars. Grounded soft curving grassy banks and a little creek in foreground; rusted maze emerges from concrete foundations, nature overgrows its edges. Distant campus/tree silhouettes as low-contrast background; layers compose coherently already, NOT an exploded layer sheet. Continuous scene from sheltered open left entry through a complex but legible rusty labyrinth to a lit right exit gap. Fine consistent PIXEL CLUSTERS and deliberate curved contours; avoid a square voxel/tile aesthetic in nature. Side elevation, not isometric, not top-down, no perspective game camera. Daylight with moss greens, warm rust, muted concrete, airy pale sky; no generic black horror ambience. Leave ample traversable spaces and light/dark separation. Entire environment composed as one finished image first, all pieces already placed; later edits/extraction will preserve its canvas and positions. No hero, enemies, professor portrait, text, logos, arrows, grids, numbered nodes, search UI or HUD. This is original concept art for discussion, not a collision-verified level. Create coherent depth and playful impossible complexity rather than isolated floating props.
prompts.background_smear_first_unselected: Use case: precise-object-edit. EDIT this complete 3:1 horizontal pixel-art scene, preserving the SAME canvas dimensions, framing, rusted maze layout, every foreground bar/platform/ladder, concrete foundation, grassy bank and foreground water. This is a visual-only renderer bug example, NOT terrain mutation. Change ONLY distant BACKGROUND vegetation/sky visible through maze openings: a horizontal band in the middle third of the image has been sampled incorrectly, so background pixels are sliced and stretched sideways into long smeared rows, with two hard scanline offsets and small repeated source strips. Think texture coordinate/sample bug applied to the backdrop itself, not a monster, lightning crack, spreading pink infection, rubble or encroaching corruption cloud. Use existing background colors; keep all active foreground silhouettes and openings readable. Localize strongest smear to center/right background openings; left entry and lower scene remain normal. No new text/404 lettering/UI/arrows, no characters, no architectural changes, no new platforms or bridges, no changed time/weather. Preserve crisp pixel language. Output one complete edited frame, same aspect ratio and camera, not a before-after collage or separate components.
prompts.background_smear_selected: Use case: precise-object-edit. Make a CLEARLY VISIBLE texture-sampling GLITCH demonstration in this exact complete scene. Preserve same 3:1 canvas and foreground rusted maze/platforms/ladders/banks/water geometry. Only the BACKGROUND visible through the rust-maze openings is corrupt. In the middle horizontal band, from about 45% to 85% of image width and about 28% to 56% of image height, REPLACE the distant forest/sky detail with VERY OBVIOUS LONG HORIZONTAL PIXEL STREAKS: source green/blue/gold pixels stretched sideways 100-250 pixels into flat scanline ribbons. There should be hard cut boundaries at top/bottom of this band and two misregistered repeated stripes. The background looks like a corrupted image buffer / bad UV sampling, NOT natural forest, NOT a subtle blur. Those sideways streaks must be unmissable even at thumbnail size. Maze bars stay drawn cleanly IN FRONT OF these corrupted background pixels, so bars occlude the effect. Foreground structure, water, lower grass and left entry remain as in input. Do not create a crack, tentacles, cloud, aura, pink infection, text, UI or new platforms. This is a VISUAL BUG in the backdrop with unchanged gameplay collision. Output ONE full-scene edited frame, not before/after comparison.
prompts.foreground_extraction_trial: Use case: background-extraction. From this already composed horizontal 3:1 pixel-art scene, extract the ENTIRE rusted maze structure (all rusted beams, concrete foundations/piers, railings, ladders and attached ivy). Preserve their exact arrangement, scale and pixel positions on the SAME full-size canvas and same camera. Remove sky, distant trees/buildings and all background visible through openings to genuine alpha transparency. Also remove foreground water and lower banks/standalone shrubs so this is only the maze/front structure plate. Keep transparent empty space where objects were, including full left margin and all maze openings; DO NOT center, enlarge, crop tightly, rearrange or redraw the maze. DO NOT produce a sprite sheet, white/black background or checkerboard painted into pixels. Output a true RGBA full-scene aligned layer, same 3:1 aspect and original canvas dimensions. This is an extraction/proof attempt from a complete approved composition, not generation of individually placed assets.
